security.scope: Original P3 byte protocol in a bounded local in-memory teaching harness with synthetic payloads only.
security.target: Learner-written CRC-framed P3 decoder and an intentionally mistaken authorization decision based solely on CRC validity.
security.environment: Unprivileged local process; at most256 synthetic input bytes per run, no network or filesystem targets.
security.attacker_capabilities: Modify payload bytes and recompute the public CRC; no keys, privileges or external access are supplied.
security.isolation: Original code and synthetic values only, bounded run, no credentials, network, production firmware or third-party target.
security.defect: Treating an unkeyed error-detection checksum as sender authentication allows attacker-selected messages to pass that mistaken authorization gate.
security.exposing_transition: Accept the known frame, flip payload00 to01 without CRC update and observe rejection, then recompute CRC and observe acceptance of0141ff by the original framing validator.
security.exploitability_limits: The violation requires the application to authorize based only on checksum validity. Framing acceptance alone is expected behavior, not a flaw in CRC. No execution, privilege or real-system compromise is claimed.
security.success_condition: A synthetic protected-value counter in the deliberately flawed teaching application changes for the recomputed unauthorized frame; no outside state is touched.
security.repair: Keep framing and authorization separate. The corrected target refuses to alter protected state in its unauthenticated mode; ordinary public framing may still accept the changed payload. If authenticated commands are required, add an independently specified keyed authentication and replay policy only after inspecting its primitive contract.
security.regression: Run original/stale-CRC/recomputed-CRC frames through flawed and corrected application gates. The corrected gate never changes protected state without authorization; ordinary framing behavior and valid CRC vectors remain unchanged.
security.residual_limits: Disabling unauthenticated protected commands contains this teaching defect but does not implement authenticated messaging. Key management, replay resistance, cryptographic primitive implementation and side channels remain separate required work for the authenticated transfer variant.
